cases.title: An extra key on the wrong property is noted, not graded as easing

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the mentor names each still_linear pair by property and time (e.g. "Scale, 0.5 s to 1.5 s is still linear. The keys at 0.5 s and 1.5 s are still diamonds") and says what to look for. It makes no set_ease call and doesn't offer to fix them.

Every name and time matches tool output: "11 keyframe pairs across 6 layers" adds up from counts (10 linear + 1 partly_eased) across Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow and Old Take; Title's four pairs and times match the snapshot; the shared 1.5 s key note follows from the demo pair; and "Scale now has 3 keys instead of 2" quotes unexpected_changes.

In turn 3 the check showed 3 still_linear pairs, and the mentor named each one with its property and times on the focus layer Title ("Position, 1.5 s → 3 s. The key at 3 s is still a diamond…", "Scale, 0.5 s → 1.5 s. Both keys are still diamonds"), said what to look for (diamonds vs hourglass shapes), and did not call set_ease or offer to fix them.

Every layer, property and time matches tool output: "11 pairs across 6 layers" adds up (10 linear + 1 partly_eased across Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow, Old Take), Subtitle Opacity stopping hard at 1.3 s matches linear_end "end" at to_time 1.3, the shared 1.5 s key note follows the demo rule, and "Title's Scale now has 3 keys instead of 2" matches unexpected_changes.

In Turn 3 the check shows 3 still_linear pairs, and the mentor names each one ("Position, 1.5 s → 3 s… Scale, 0.5 s → 1.5 s… Opacity, 0.5 s → 1.5 s") and what to look for (diamonds, select both keys, F9); it makes no set_ease call and doesn't offer to fix them.
